note:
An engraved portrait plate, lettered “IEROM. MACARIE” and signed in the plate “V. Damian sculp. 1908, Bucuresci”. Fetched 2026-08-28 from byzantion.ro at 600x817, where it illustrates the article “Macarie Ieromonahul (1750-1836)” with no caption and no credit of its own; the source_url is that file, because it is where this copy was actually taken and a link a reader can check is worth more than a tidier one that was not used. **The plate is almost certainly from Nicolae M. Popescu, „Viața și activitatea dascălului de cântări Macarie Ieromonahul”, București, 1908** — the year on the signature and the year of that monograph agree, and it is the standard study — but that identification is inferred here and is not asserted by the page this copy came from.

Licence: the engraving is a flat two-dimensional work and this is a faithful photographic reproduction of it, which acquires no copyright of its own (EU Directive 2019/790 Article 14, which Romania has implemented). What the reproduction cannot do is outlive the original, and the original is a *signed* 1908 engraving rather than an ancient icon: it is in the public domain if V. Damian died before 1956. That is likely for a Bucharest engraver working in 1908 and it is not established here. Recorded so that whoever revisits this knows which part is checked and which is inferred.

Cropped locally, 2026-08-28, from 600x817 to 600x715: the fetched scan carried the book's printed caption below the plate — „portarie al sfinteĭ Mitropoliĭ din Bucurescĭ (1780 saŭ 1785—1845)” — and the hero's top 3:2 crop is taken from the figure, so the caption was two lines of type sitting under the picture on a card. Nothing outside the crop is lost from the corpus: the full scan, caption included, is at the source_url above. **That caption's dates are not this record's dates and disagree with them** — see the note on `dates` in saint.json.

At 600 px wide this is narrower than most icons in the corpus, which were fetched at 1200. It is enough for a card and for the hero at one column; a better scan of the 1908 plate would be worth taking if one is found.
